newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish depo mkt dry, zloty inches up vs basket.
newsitem.headline: Polish depo mkt dry, zloty inches up vs basket.

text.p: Poland's money market was dry in early Monday trade with rates high above the central bank's lombard rate of 25 percent as many banks let out cash in 14-day drainages in April and were now short of funds, dealers said.
"Many banks had surpluses at the end of April reserve so they let the cash out in 14-day central bank reverse repos, and are now short," said Krzysztof Chmura of Bank Gdanski SA.

At 0845 GMT overnight and tomorrow/next rates were at 24.90/26.00 percent against the opening's 24.9/25.8 percent and 24.7/25.5 percent respectively. The National Bank of Poland refrained from all market operations.

On the forex market the zloty was idle just below the NBP-established intervention level of 2.5 percent from the trading band centre and dealers did not it to go higher because it would meet a central bank intervention.
"The zloty is likely to stay at the NBP resistance because everybody knows that if it goes any higher the central bank will step in," said Malgorzata Sawicka of Bank Handlowy SA.

At 0855 GMT the zloty was at 2.49/2.48 against the parity rate from 2.49/2.44 percent at opening. It was at 3.1625/28 against the dollar from 3.1625/40 at opening and 1.8310/14 against the mark from 1.8309/19 at opening.

Dealers said the zloty would not see much help from foreign investment in Polish T-bills at today's 1.4 billion zloty primary tender as demand from abroad was seen small because of a market holiday in London.

"Most of foreign investors go through London which is closed today, and many of those who will bid any way already have zlotys on accounts, so their forex impact may be small," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, T-bill dealer at Bank Handlowy.
